panels.rationale: Real patient coronal CT abdomen image from a Rabson-Mendenhall syndrome case report, showing bilateral nephromegaly and nephrocalcinosis which are supported disease-specific renal findings in the provided vocabulary. The image includes a red box annotation, has no visible skin, and no other diseases or non-patient content are present.
panels.attribution_text: Chong et al. Renal manifestations of severe Rabson-Mendenhall syndrome: a case report.. Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders 2013. doi:10.1186/2251-6581-12-7. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Renal manifestations on CT abdomen. Bilateral nephromegaly (Greater than 2 standard deviation for age), and nephrocalcinosis (in red box).
in_text_mentions: idney of 12.3 cm, left kidney of 13.2 cm, with multiple bilateral renal calculi, the largest 10mm in diameter. The right renal pelvis was dilated (1.2 cm), and a simple 10 mm cyst seen in the left kidney. The bladder was normal. A CT urogram revealed a 2 mm calcification seen to the left of the true renal pelvis, suggestive of an intraluminal ureteric calculus. Intravenous pyelogram further demonstrated paintbrush-like appearances of the renal pyramids, consistent with MSK (Figure 2). The patient had the most severe form of MSK, grade 4, with involvement of all the calyces in both kidneys [8].

findings.label: Generalized hypertrichosis
findings.evidence: visual: increased terminal hair growth on face and neck

panels.rationale: Clinical photograph of a child with Rabson-Mendenhall syndrome demonstrating characteristic coarse facial features, florid acanthosis nigricans on the neck and chest, and generalized hypertrichosis, consistent with the disease presentation described in the article.
panels.attribution_text: Sinnarajah et al. Rabson Mendenhall Syndrome caused by a novel missense mutation.. International journal of pediatric endocrinology 2016. doi:10.1186/s13633-016-0039-1. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
in_text_mentions: On examination he weighed 17.5 kg (-3SD), his height was 111 cm (-6SD), head circumference 47 cm (-3SD), weight for height was -1SD to –2SD indicating significant growth failure. Facial dysmorphism characterized by small head, large ears, broad nose, prognathism, malocclusion of teeth were noted along with prominent nipples. There was extensive acanthosis nigricans, hypertrichosis, thick finger nails and coarse hands (Figs. 1 and 2).Fig. 1Coarse facies Fig. 2Acanthosis nigricans and hypertrichosis

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Clinical photograph of the neck/axilla showing confluent hyperpigmented velvety plaques consistent with florid acanthosis nigricans, a classic cutaneous manifestation of Rabson-Mendenhall syndrome in the reported 5-year-old pediatric patient. B: Clinical photograph of the abdomen showing acrochordons, protruberant abdomen, and lipohypertrophy, all listed as clinical manifestations of Rabson-Mendenhall syndrome in the figure caption for the reported pediatric patient. C: Clinical photograph of the arm showing increased terminal hair growth (hypertrichosis), a typical clinical manifestation of Rabson-Mendenhall syndrome in the reported pediatric patient. D: Clinical photograph of the oral cavity showing dysplastic teeth with dental caries, consistent with premature eruption of dysplastic teeth, a typical dental manifestation of Rabson-Mendenhall syndrome in the reported pediatric patient. in_text_mentions: A five year old female presented, shortly after migration from Africa, with chronic scalp infection and otitis media. She was noted to have symptomatic hyperglycaemia, with a history dating back possibly to two years of age. She was observed to have several cutaneous and facial features typical of the RMS phenotype (Figure 1).

plate_findings.evidence: Caption states 'thick nails'; visual shows markedly thickened nail plate on thumb

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Clinical photograph of both hands in a patient with Rabson-Mendenhall syndrome showing broad, large thumbs. Caption states 'big, broad thumbs' and in-text mentions 'large, broad thumbs.' Article title directly supports RMS diagnosis. Broad thumbs are a characteristic finding of RMS though not present in the provided vocabulary. B: Clinical photograph showing thick dystrophic nail in a patient with Rabson-Mendenhall syndrome. Caption directly states 'thick nails.' Matches vocabulary finding for dystrophic thick nails. Article title confirms RMS diagnosis.
